title: Monarch structured FFN views over shared weights
hypothesis: A small Monarch factor code over one shared FFN can represent aligned task functions at lower serialized bytes than independent dense maps; simple factor coefficients may fully explain any Mirror effect, and independent maps test private-state need.
physical_object: one frozen 16×16 shared linear FFN map
mirror_coordinate: per-task coefficient on shared Monarch block-diagonal/permutation factor direction

development.allowed: validate exact structured decode, fit, serialization, runtime and fresh freeze

success_gate: Aligned task NRMSE <=0.01 and payload <=70% of native per-task Monarch; Mirror-specific claim requires >=10% improvement over generic scalar at matched bytes.
failure_gate: NRMSE >0.05 or <20% byte saving at matched quality; generic scalar equivalence means no Mirror-specific gain.
amendments: Development audit found the teacher shared a common Monarch transform plus task scalar, while the physical baseline omitted the common transform. Before fresh, incorporated the common factor into the paid shared W and retained only the task variation in the scalar code. The code fit is closed-form support-only least squares and identical for Mirror/generic controls.
boundaries: Logical code combinations do not imply independent capacity
